Young people lead this work.

Catalyst for Change Organization is a youth-led, non-political and non-profit organization. It began in 2022 as the Zatonse Youth Club in Thembedza, Traditional Authority Makhwira, and was established as C.4.C in March 2025.

Our founders set out to answer the challenges facing young people around them: limited access to education, unemployment, environmental degradation, low SRHR awareness and gender inequality. We believe development does not rest in the hands of elders alone.

Our mission

To equip young people and marginalized individuals with practical skills, mentorship and innovative solutions that promote self-reliance, active civic engagement and sustainable community development.

Our vision

A transformed and inclusive community where youths and disadvantaged individuals are empowered with skills, opportunities and innovations for sustainable development.

What we do

Three projects, one aim: keep young people learning, healthy and heard.

Education and mentorship

Nzeru 4 Change

Physical mentorship sessions and career guidance in primary and secondary schools, led by live role models who are proud residents of the communities we serve.

Sport, health and rights

Champions 4 Change

We use the power of sport to create safe spaces where young people can talk about education, comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) and SRHR. We work with 3 primary schools in Chikwawa.

Education support

Education Support Program

Needy but deserving students receive school basic needs and scholarships, so that poverty does not decide who stays in class.

Where our work reaches

We work across seven thematic areas, through school clubs, youth clubs, faith groups and community dialogues.

Education and mentorshipHealth: SRHR, HIV and AIDS, nutrition, mental healthGender equality and good governanceEnvironment and climate resilienceEntrepreneurship and livelihood skillsYouth leadership and policy advocacyChild protection and social inclusion

Our schools and sites include Ole Ole, Nyakamba and Mitondo Primary Schools, Mitole Resource Centre, Mitondo and Livunzu Secondary Schools, and Mitondo Health Centre for youth-friendly health services.

C.4.C is governed by a Board of Trustees drawn from agriculture, education, health, gender and entrepreneurship. It is registered at district level through the Chikwawa District Council and District Youth Office, and its registration under the Trustees Incorporation Act and the NYCOM Act is in progress.

Where we work

Our secretariat is based in Chikwawa, and our volunteers run school and youth clubs across Traditional Authority Makhwira, including the Livunzu zone. We hope to extend to more schools across the district as resources allow.
